overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 12
overview.text: This lesson builds on students' work from Grade 8 and their work with bivariate data and its relationships. Previous studies of relationships have primarily focused on linear models. For this lesson, students begin their work with nonlinear relationships, specifically exponential and quadratic models.
outcomes: Students distinguish between scatter plots that display a relationship that can be reasonably modeled by a linear equation and those that should be modeled by a nonlinear equation.
overview.teacherInsight: Emphasize precise mathematical definitions and multiple problem-solving representations. Encourage students to check the reasonableness of their numerical solutions.

exitTicket.title: Lesson 12 Exit Ticket: Relationships Between Two Numerical Variables
exitTicket.prompt:
Exit Ticket

You are traveling around the United States with friends. After spending a day in a town that is 2,000 ft. above sea level, you plan to spend the next several days in a town that is 5,000 ft. above sea level. Is this town likely to have more or fewer clear days per year than the town that is 2,000 ft. above sea level? Explain your answer.

You plan to buy a bike helmet. Based on data presented in this lesson, will buying the most expensive bike helmet give you a helmet with the highest quality rating? Explain your answer.

Data Source: www.consumerreports.org/health

You are traveling around the United States with friends. After spending a day in a town that is 2,000 ft. above sea level, you plan to spend the next several days in a town that is 5,000 ft. above sea level. Is this town likely to have more or fewer clear days per year than the town that is 2,000 ft. above sea level? Explain your answer.

I would expect the number of clear days per year to increase. The relationship between elevation above sea level and the mean number of clear days per year appears to be linear. The scatter plot indicates that as the elevation increases, the number of clear days per year also generally increases.

You plan to buy a bike helmet. Based on data presented in this lesson, will buying the most expensive bike helmet give you a helmet with the highest quality rating? Explain your answer.

Data Source: www.consumerreports.org/health

I think there is a good chance I would not be buying the bike helmet with the highest price. The scatter plot indicates that there is no relationship between price and quality rating.

problemSet.title: Official Worksheet: Problem Set & Practice
problemSet.description: Master Relationships Between Two Numerical Variables through authentic curriculum practice problems. Check your work using the expandable teacher solution key below.

problems.prompt: Construct a scatter plot that displays the data for x (elevation above sea level in feet) and w (mean number of partly cloudy days per year).
problems.solution: Provide students with graph paper or have students construct the scatter plot using a graphing calculator or graphing software. The following represents the scatter plot.

problems.prompt: Based on the scatter plot you constructed in Problem 1, is there a relationship between elevation and the mean number of partly cloudy days per year? If so, how would you describe the relationship? Explain your reasoning.
problems.solution: There appears to be a relationship. As the elevation increases, the number of partly cloudy days tends to decrease from approximately 0 to 3,000 ft. above sea level. Then at approximately 3,000 ft. above sea level, as the elevation increases, the number of partly cloudy days also appears to increase. This pattern suggests a quadratic model. Some cities, however, do not follow this pattern. (Students should discuss the overall pattern.)

Scatter Plot 5

Data Source: Elissa Z. Cameron, Kevin J. Stafford, Wayne L. Linklater, and Clare J. Veltman, "Suckling behaviour does not measure milk intake in horses, equus caballus," Animal Behaviour, 57 (1999): 673.

A mare is a female horse, and a foal is a baby horse. Is there a relationship between a foal's birth weight and a mare's weight, or are the data points scattered?

If there is a relationship between baby birth weight and mother's weight, does the relationship look linear?
problems.solution:
If there is a relationship between baby birth weight and mother's weight, does the relationship look linear?

The relationship does look linear. As the mare's weight increases, the foal birth weight tends to increase.
